- [FACT] The glutes are described as the big muscles that constitute most of the butt.

- [FACT] The gluteal muscles are a group of three muscles that make up the buttocks.
- [FACT] The piriformis is mentioned as a smaller muscle in the gluteal area.
- [FACT] Functions of gluteal muscles include: helping to stand up, maintaining erect posture, preventing forward falls while walking or running, keeping the pelvis stable, assisting in rising from a seated position, picking things up, climbing stairs, skiing, running, rowing, and making love.
- [FACT] The glutes are described as some of the most important muscles in the body.
- [FACT] When glutes are inactive, the spine bears the brunt of forces, leading to potential damage.
- [FACT] The tiny muscles around the spine can become strained and fail when glutes are inactive.
- [FACT] The psoas muscles may become tighter when glutes are inactive, increasing pressure on the spine.
- [FACT] Micro irritations over time can lead to macro damage to the spine.
- [FACT] The author emphasizes that waking up the glutes is crucial for healing back pain.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant summarizes the importance of reversing gluteal inactivity to heal back pain.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant outlines three steps to address gluteal inactivity: wake up your glutes, make them strong, and learn to use them appropriately.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant introduces the "clamshell" exercise as a method to wake up and strengthen the glutes.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant provides detailed steps for performing the clamshell exercise:
  - Step 1: Lie on your side with hips and knees bent.
  - Step 2: Use the thumb of the top hand to dig inside the upper hip bone.
  - Step 3: Lay the four fingers of that hand across the outside of the hip.
  - Step 4: Feel the gluteal muscles with your fingers to reestablish the connection with your brain.
  - Step 5: Find your neutral spine and brace your core.
